summary: 1. Top stayed videos (66.9% - 67.6%) use direct counter-intuitive statements or vivid physical analogies in the first sentence ('jo car crash me pichak jaati hai, wo tumhe zyaada bachati hai' or 'daanto par 3 chhoti cars') rather than explanatory questions. 2. The top-performing titles are punchy, short Devanagari Hindi questions under 9 words focused on visceral or tangible topics like car crashes and T-rex bite force, avoiding formal English phrasing. 3. Bottom third videos by both views (<35) and stayed percentage (<30%) rely on passive documentary setups, Romanized Hindi, or academic curiosity ('kyun mili hain', 'Common Household Items') that trigger immediate swipe-aways. 4. Videos with stayed_pct > 60% immediately cross 1,300+ views into algorithmic circulation, whereas videos below 40% stayed_pct stall under 100 views regardless of retention length. 5. Video duration target must stay ultra-lean (15–25 seconds total) because top videos achieve high engagement within 14–15 seconds average view duration, while 40-50+ second scripts fail to hold early interest.
winning_hooks: जो car crash में पिचक जाती है, वो तुम्हें ज़्यादा बचाती है। (Direct paradox statement that immediately contradicts intuition)
सोचो, तुम्हारे दांतों पर 3 छोटी cars एक के ऊपर एक रख दी जाएं। इतने ज़ोर से T. rex काटता था। (Visceral physical scale comparison that creates instant imagery)
avoid: Vague English titles and academic topic phrasings like 'Common Household Items That Contain Radioactive Materials' or 'The hidden engineering of...'
Opening hooks structured as academic or passive questions (e.g., '...kyun mili hain jo khoon ki koshikaon jaisi dikhti hain?' or '...swad kyun deta hai?')
Scripts extending beyond 40 seconds before mastering the initial 3-second hold rate
Mixing Romanized Hindi/Urdu script into titles and hooks instead of crisp Devanagari or clean Hinglish keywords
next_experiment: A/B test Hook Structure on the same topic: Script A opens with a direct counter-intuitive statement ('Airbag tumhe bachaane ke liye explode karta hai, soft pillow nahi hota'), versus Script B opening with an interrogative question ('Kya aapko pata hai airbag kaise bachta hai?'), keeping both under 20 seconds and tracking if Script A breaks the 65% stayed_pct threshold.
